locked_findings.title: Telegram runtime deployment is coupled to the mutable development worktree
locked_findings.summary: The Telegram runtime deployment path depends on the mutable development checkout, allowing legitimate development state to block canonical convergence and automatic recovery.

locked_findings.title: Restored non-canonical Development Recovery content can cross into the credential-bearing Telegram runtime through the shared development ROOT
locked_findings.summary: Development Recovery correctly prevents recovery/dev/** from directly triggering deployment, but restore() can materialize non-canonical source into the same mutable ROOT from which Telegram start/restart/foreground execute.
locked_findings.distinction: Non-canonical recovery material crossing into a credential-bearing runtime.
additional_evidence: An already-running Telegram gateway can lazily import repository modules from the shared ROOT after restore(), without an explicit runtime restart. telegram_conversation_service performs function-local imports for harness_mission_execution_router and telegram_hermes_dispatch_service.

CapabilityAdapter resolves Registry executor bindings at execution time through resolve_registry_executor(), which uses importlib.import_module(module_name). A restored module not already present in sys.modules can therefore become executable in the live credential-bearing process on a later normal request.
Observed lazy-loaded dispatch services can produce external side effects, including GitHub Actions workflow_dispatch via GitHubActionsDispatcher.
locked_findings.scope_qualification: This expands the observed reachability of F002 beyond explicit start/restart/foreground. It does not create a distinct violated invariant, so no additional finding is opened from this path at present.

locked_findings.title: Development Recovery scans and digests live worktree bytes before staging potentially different bytes, allowing a DURABLE recovery tree to diverge from content_digest and bypass the recovery secret-scan boundary
locked_findings.causal_statement: persist() performs path/secret scanning and content_digest computation through separate reads of the mutable worktree, then later stages those paths into a temporary Git index without freezing the byte set or revalidating the staged blobs. A mutation between those phases can therefore cause the recovery tree to contain bytes different from those represented by the recorded content_digest. Because recovery-path secret scanning occurs only during the earlier read and is not repeated against the exact staged blobs or resulting tree, secret-like content introduced during that window can bypass that barrier and be included in the recovery commit while remote tree readback still succeeds and the checkpoint reaches DURABLE.

impact.qualification: Secret exposure is a directly reachable consequence of the same code path but remains labeled potential until reproduced by a dedicated secret-like mutation test.

locked_findings.distinction: Non-atomic recovery snapshot capture; validated/digested bytes are not guaranteed to equal committed/pushed bytes.

locked_findings.title: Development Continuity defines a 300 s RPO target and 600 s hard maximum but has no observed closed-loop monitor enforcing elapsed time since the last verified remote checkpoint
locked_findings.causal_statement: The continuity policy contains correct decision logic for WATCHDOG events, including mandatory checkpointing at the 600-second hard maximum, but no runtime component observed in the audited HEAD calculates elapsed time from the last independently verified remote checkpoint, periodically invokes that policy, or alerts/blocks when the hard maximum is exceeded. The 90-second heartbeat is intentionally liveness-only, so dirty development state can remain beyond the declared RPO hard maximum without automatic detection or enforcement when no qualifying semantic checkpoint event occurs.
locked_findings.impact: Primary impact is loss of recent development progress and violation of a declared durability/RPO guarantee. No unauthorized execution or direct secret exposure is implied.
locked_findings.distinction: RPO policy exists, but closed-loop operational enforcement is not observed.

locked_findings.title: Development Recovery classifies large evidence by a narrow path/extension allowlist with no size threshold, allowing large or non-source artifacts in unrecognized formats under recoverable source paths to be committed inline
locked_findings.causal_statement: Development Recovery correctly excludes bytes for artifacts classified as LARGE_EVIDENCE, but classification depends only on a fixed set of path prefixes and file extensions and applies no byte-size threshold. Files under recoverable source roots that use unrecognized media, archive, database, model, dataset, or binary formats can therefore be treated as normal recoverable source and committed into recovery/dev/** despite the normative requirement that large media and evidence remain locator-only.
locked_findings.impact: Observed defect: violation of the locator-only durability boundary. Expected operational consequences include repository growth and increased checkpoint latency or push failure as object sizes grow. Potential exposure of sensitive binary/media material exists but is not claimed as demonstrated.
locked_findings.preferred_control: Path/type policy + explicit byte-size ceiling + exact-byte sensitivity inspection; do not rely only on filename extensions.
locked_findings.distinction: The correctly classified LARGE_EVIDENCE path remains locator-only; the defect is incomplete capture-time classification/size enforcement.

non_findings.candidate: Git-ref interference between Development Continuity and Telegram runtime
non_findings.reason: Remote recovery-ref writer fencing remains robust: EXPECTED_PREVIOUS_REMOTE_OID, non-force push, explicit recovery ref targeting, and independent remote readback are not bypassed by the Telegram supervisor.

non_findings.candidate: Automatic promotion of Development Recovery commits/content into the canonical branch
non_findings.reason: No automatic recovery-to-canonical promotion path was observed. Development checkpoint persistence rejects PROMOTION and is scoped to recovery/dev/**. The permanent canonical promotion workflow is workflow_dispatch-only, accepts only refs/heads/staging/security-* as staging_ref, requires exact old/candidate/tree binding, trusted Harness authorization plus SecurityReviewReceipt evidence, fast-forward ancestry, and uses the dedicated deploy-key identity. Active repository rulesets protect work/gate6f-analytics-learning and expose no user/repository-role/admin bypass.

non_findings.candidate: Separate residual side-effect finding for live lazy-loading of restored recovery content
non_findings.reason: The live-runtime lazy-import path is real code-level evidence, but it violates the same authority/plane-isolation invariant already captured by F002. It broadens F002 reachability beyond explicit restart rather than constituting an independent finding.

audit_notes.telegram_project_isolation: BR-no-GTA and Hazewave Telegram systems are separate projects and must not share bot tokens, config roots, state roots, supervisors, deployment roots, recovery state, or authority.
audit_notes.current_scope: This file records findings for BR-1 only and does not assert remediation or closure.
